questions.q: How does the Claude API signal that a tool_result represents a failure rather than a success?
options: By setting is_error: true on the tool_result block, alongside the usual content
By omitting the tool_use_id entirely
By sending a separate error-type message instead of a tool_result
There is no way to signal an error — failures are silently ignored
questions.explain: A failed call is still a normal tool_result block, just with is_error: true set so Claude knows to treat the content as a failure, not a success.

questions.q: According to this lesson's guidance, what's wrong with an error message like just "failed" or "error"?
options: Nothing — short error messages are always preferred
It's too long and wastes tokens
It leaves Claude no better informed than before the call, instead of a message that explains what went wrong and what to try next
The API rejects any error message under 10 characters
questions.explain: A specific message like 'Rate limit exceeded. Retry after 60 seconds.' gives Claude the context to recover or adapt; a bare 'failed' doesn't.

questions.q: When Claude's own tool call is invalid (e.g., missing a required parameter), what does Claude typically do after receiving an is_error tool_result explaining the problem?
options: It immediately terminates the entire conversation
It typically retries 2-3 times with corrections before apologizing to the user
It ignores the error and repeats the exact same invalid call forever
It automatically switches to a completely different, unrelated tool
questions.explain: Per Anthropic's documentation, Claude treats a clear invalid-call error as something it can self-correct from, retrying a few times with fixes before giving up.

questions.q: What does setting strict: true on a tool definition actually guarantee?
options: That the external API or service behind the tool will never go down
That tool inputs will always match the defined schema exactly, eliminating missing parameters and type mismatches
That the tool will run twice as fast
That Claude will never need to see an error message again, for any reason
questions.explain: strict tool use prevents malformed calls at the schema level, but it does nothing for execution errors like a real API being unavailable — those still need is_error handling.

questions.q: If a particular tool keeps receiving invalid calls from Claude during development, what does this lesson suggest is usually the real problem?
options: The tool's description likely needs work, per Lesson 6's guidance, rather than needing more error-handling code to paper over it
The Claude API is fundamentally broken and unusable
The model has a hardware fault that requires restarting
Nothing can be done — invalid calls are random and unrelated to tool design
questions.explain: A pattern of invalid calls is a signal connecting back to Lesson 6: a vague or ambiguous description is often the actual root cause, not a gap in error handling.
